message.content:
Research COMPANIES for cold outreach, not job postings. Return data only, no commentary.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Prabhavit Gupta, based in VENICE, ITALY, already resident with full right to work, so Italian companies need no relocation and no sponsorship at all. This is his cheapest possible win.
CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: he speaks ENGLISH ONLY, with no working Italian. Most Italian companies operate in Italian. So the whole value of this lane is finding the Italian companies where ENGLISH IS GENUINELY THE WORKING LANGUAGE: internationally funded scale-ups, companies with a foreign founder or a distributed team, Italian offices of international companies, and Italian companies whose careers pages and engineering blogs are written in English. Say for each one what your evidence is that they work in English. If your only evidence is that a marketing page has an English version, say so, because that is weak evidence.
~3 years experience. At FlowSpace, a coworking booking platform grown 2,000 to 4,500+ users, he built AI support agents, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, outbound and sales-funnel automation, a scraping and parsing pipeline, and integrations with Office RnD, Nexudus and Clubee. He led a Bubble.io to Next.js and Laravel migration on the live product.
Stack: n8n (deep), OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, Make, Zapier, Airtable, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js, Laravel and PHP, Supabase, Postgres, REST APIs and webhooks, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate (certified).
Targets EUR 30,000-40,000 salary, or EUR 200/day as an Italian sole trader with an individual Partita IVA (no limited company). Note that an Italian client can engage his Partita IVA with no friction at all, which is a real selling point in this lane.

TWO OUTREACH MODES, tag every company with one or both:
- "speculative job": a direct approach could create or surface a role.
- "freelance client": they would plausibly BUY n8n / AI automation / integration work at around EUR 200 a day.

YOUR LANE: Italy. Cover Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna, Florence, Padua, Venice, Verona, Trento, Naples, and remote-Italy companies. Look at:
- Italian scale-ups with international VC funding and English-language engineering culture.
- Italian offices of international technology companies.
- Italian coworking and flexspace operators, since that is his domain: Talent Garden, Copernico, LVenture, Impact Hub Italy and others you find.
- Italian e-commerce, logistics, travel, hospitality and fintech companies large enough to have an automation problem but too small to have an internal automation team.
- Italian digital agencies and software houses that serve international clients in English.
Note that it.linkedin.com is robots-disallowed, so use other sources.

FOR EACH COMPANY RETURN
- what they actually do, in one line
- your EVIDENCE that they work in English, specifically
- the SPECIFIC reason he is unusual for them, tied to something real he built. Generic praise is useless.
- the best route in. He will reach people on LinkedIn, so give the exact JOB TITLE to search for at that company plus the company's LinkedIn page URL. Name a specific person ONLY if their name and role are publicly published on the company's own site or a press page, and say where you saw it. NEVER invent or guess an email address or a person. If the company publishes a general contact email on its own website, include it verbatim.
- what he should lead with in the first message, one sentence, concrete.
- watch-outs, and be honest when the Italian-language risk is high.

RULES
- Companies must currently exist and be active. Check.
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Plain hyphens only.
- Never invent a URL, a person, an email or a funding figure. If you do not know, write "not stated".
- Do NOT return these, already covered: Satispay, Musixmatch, Moneyfarm, Docplanner, MioDottore, Reverse, Loomya, DADA ENERGY, MailerLite, Trustfull, Lexroom, Nebulay, Nebulab, Treatwell, ShippyPro, Nozomi Networks, Arkipel, Pinnipedia, Jamie, telmi.

OUTPUT: ONLY a JSON array, no prose before or after:
{"company":"","what":"","hq":"","size":"","mode":"speculative job|freelance client|both","why_him":"","english_evidence":"","route_in":"","linkedin":"","public_email":"","lead_with":"","watch_outs":"","source":""}
Aim for 14 to 18 companies.
